Title: Two-Factor Authentication Setup
FAQ: How do I set up two-factor authentication?

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to your account. To enable 2FA, go to Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication and click Enable. We support authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) and SMS verification. Authenticator apps are recommended over SMS for stronger security. After enabling 2FA, you will be prompted for a verification code at each login.
--- End Document 1 ---

Title: Security Policy
Information Security Policy

Passwords must be changed every 90 days. Never reuse the last 5 passwords. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for all accounts with administrative privileges. Users must lock their workstations when away from their desks.

final_answer:
Multi-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to accounts by requiring multiple credentials for authentication. 2FA typically involves using a combination of two or more of the following:

- **Knowledge-based factors:** Something you know, such as a password or PIN.
- **Possession-based factors:** Something you have, like a physical token or smartphone.
- **Biometric factors:** Something you are, such as a fingerprint or facial scan.

The retrieved documents explain that 2FA is commonly implemented through authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) or SMS verification. By requiring multiple credentials, 2FA significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized access even if one credential is compromised.

- Document 1 & 2: Two-Factor Authentication Setup FAQs
- Document 4: Security Policy - Information Security Policy
